text: and into resolveShot's own y=0 ground plane (shamble-core.js:1507); aimGround is used only when nothing is hit within 400 m (1128). So open ground is aimed at height 0, but platform and building tops are aimed at their own height and ramps at the top of their bounding box, above the slope (probe through tools/preview.js eval on the default map, a downward ray through the SIM: it stops at 1.20, 2.50 and 4.00 m on the three platforms, and at 2.50 m on a ramp whose slope there is 1.25 m). Only the throwVelocity users (grenades, Molotovs and the bow: heading to aimGround, 1711) and the Juggernaut cannon (aimGround + 0.6 m, 1304) still aim at the y=0 ground point, so LOOP_V2 §9's 'today the cursor aims at the ground' holds for those only;

find: The client sends an aim direction; the server re-resolves the shot.
text: Legacy aims at a world point, not a direction: each pellet's direction is aimPoint minus playerFireOrigin (1473), and aimPoint is the camera ray's hit in the SIM as the client sees it (1126-1129). So the v2 command should carry the quantised aim point (or the camera ray) with the client's view time; the server rebuilds the direction from its own fire origin and re-resolves the shot against the world rewound to that time. A bare direction would shift the shot by any correction of the fire origin.

Found in code and measured: fire cooldowns are reset, not carried (ps.fireCd=interval at 1471 after the decrement at 2690; bots the same at 2913), so every fire interval rounds up to whole frames. Probe on the real update() (tools/preview.js eval, Shabzon held for 10 game seconds): 10.0 / 12.0 / 13.1 shots per second at 30 / 60 / 144 Hz, against 13.9 from its table value (0.072 s); that matches 3, 5 and 11 frames per shot. The legacy feel was tuned at whatever frame rate the tester had; on a fixed v2 tick the table values only hold if cooldowns carry their remainder, as acquireTarget already does for scans (1597). The tick-rate choice (R2) must account for it.
